properties.description:
BACKGROUND:
Two vacant NR3 lots totaling 9,426 SF are part of the Office of Planning and Community Development's proposed "Centers & Corridors" zoning change to LR3 along 35th Avenue SW in West Seattle. The two existing lots flank an existing alley right of way, platted over a hundred years ago but remaining unimproved. The alley right of way currently joins the busy 35th Avenue SW arterial at an acute angle.

 PROPOSAL:
We are proposing lot boundary adjustments to relocate and reorient the alley right of way perpendicular to 35th Avenue SW (.making it much safer for turning traffic), reconfiguration of the shape of the two existing lots (.affecting Seattle Parks Department and Seattle Department of Transportation properties), and, assuming approval of OPCD rezoning efforts along 35th Avenue SW, consolidation of the two existing lots now separated by the alley ROW allowing them, once together, to be more practical for five story, LR3 multi-family development.

properties.description:
Cascade Public Media (CPM), a prominent local media organization, is embarking on an exciting venture as they relocate to their new headquarters located at 316 Broadway. This building was originally constructed by Childhaven, a school dedicated to nurturing young minds. The property is currently zoned as MR(M), which imposes certain restrictions on signage, particularly limiting them to a maximum height of 15 feet. However, with CPM's vision for the building, the team is keen to explore the possibility of obtaining a zoning variance that would enable the installation of a distinctive wall sign on the south-facing upper story of this impressive 5-story structure.

The decision to seek a zoning variance for signage is driven by the building's transformation into a commercial office space, complete with a first-floor event area. This shift in function and the building's importance within the community make it essential for CPM to align its signage with its new role effectively. To accomplish this, CPM is aiming to have its signage proposal reviewed under the NC3 sign code. The NC3 zoning classification is well-suited for properties in the surrounding area and has the flexibility needed to accommodate signage that complements the building's use as both a commercial office space and a venue for community events.

By pursuing this zoning variance and aligning their signage with the NC3 code, CPM demonstrates their commitment to both preserving the building's historical significance and adapting it to serve the evolving needs of the community. This move not only reflects CPM's dedication to their mission but also underscores their desire to create a welcoming and distinctive presence in the heart of the community while respecting the building's storied past.

properties.description:
Application in response to Shoreline NOV 1055818-VI
Gypsum to Gypsum (GTG) is a recycling company located at 816 S Kenyon St. Seattle, WA 98108. Our company is the only processing company for recycled gypsum in the state of Washington and plays a critical role in keeping drywall from ending up in King County landfills according to the landfill ban policy in King County. The site we are operating on has a shoreline overlay that allows recycling however has a water dependence aspect it. However, the waterway is unnavigable because the Army Corps of Engineers has not up kept that area where the dock is located. We are applying for a master use permit with a variance to permit the site to continued to be used for industrial recycling activities but allows us to do so without the need for water dependence.

properties.description:
This building built in 1926 has a non-conforming use as a triplex in a single family zone.  This non-conforming use as a triplex is based on an electrical permit from the 1960s.  Owner wishes to update the zoning on this property to reflect current codes.  Per owner's understanding, owner believes that this property could be converted to a single family residence with two ADUs.  Owner lives in the largest unit which is considered the main residence.  The other two units, which owner wishes to convert to ADUs, were recently renovated (2010 for one unit and 2011 for the other unit) under permits.  As a result owner believes that these units should pass most if not all permit requirements in order to establish these two units as legal ADUs.  

However, currently two of the units have entrances that are street facing (the main unit and what is currently known as Unit #3). When Unit #3 was renovated in 2010, under City of Seattle permits, a new entry for Unit #3 was created within the existing building envelope.  Prior to the renovation, the building space which was to become the new entry for Unit #3 was an additional entry for the main unit.  Hence the building always had two entrances facing the street (see attached 1969 photo of house). Further, the new entrance for Unit #3 is visible as a black gate from the street.  When the gate is opened, there are stairs that lead up to Unit #3 and the main door for Unit #3, which is not visible from the street.

properties.description:
Temporary Use for one day event TYPE I construction permit; not TYPE II land use to allow more that 1,000 attendees to event per conditioning on previous permit. slm LU Intake

Applicant narrative: 
 I was advised via your email service to apply for a "temporary land use permit".  Seattle Children's Book Festival is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization looking to hold a free community event on the Ingraham High School grounds.  Ingraham High has a master use permit that the city issued them that states that when the field, auditorium and gym are all scheduled, they can only have a maximum total on site of 1,000 attendees and participants for events due to the parking.  We are looking for a temporary use permit that would allow us to exceed that.  Our event is likely to have approximately 7,000 attendees (a max of around 3,000 at any given time).  It would be a one time event on Saturday August 8th, 2020 open to the public from 11am to 4pm.  The Seattle School District Property Managers are concerned because -- in their words:  "the adjacent neighbors formed a coalition and filed an appeal for the construction of the field and the Hearing Examiner conditioned our permit for the facility. Part of that agreement with the adjacent neighbors that we would not schedule multiple events. This is a standard agreement we have at four of our schools. It would be up to you to get a waiver in writing from SDCI saying you are exempt from the ruling of the Hearing Examiner for the project construction."  When I shared this via your email Q and A service they suggested that a "Temporary Land Use Permit" from SDCI would satisfy that Seattle Public Schools requirement.  

I made my best guesses to the Project Information questions below.  Thank you!

properties.description:
LU - Short Plat - Divide two existing parcels, located at 5010 and 5020 NE 45th St. Seattle, (Parcel Nos. 5364200715 & 5364200721), 
and totaling 57,903 sq. ft., into 6 single family residential lots ranging in size from 7,000 sq. ft. to 11,500 sq. ft.. The property is zoned SF5000.  The site contains on large 6,430 sq. ft. single family home, which will be demolished. There are approximately 11 significant trees and 18 exceptional trees on the site, which will be removed and replanted.


Questions for Pre Application:
1) Review Short Plat process.  Confirm SEPA and Design Review Exempt? Neighborhood meeting?
2) The site contains 11 significant trees and 18 exceptional trees. The project proposes to removal all trees and replant.  How SMC 25.11 and other tree related regulations be implemented? Replanting?
3) There appears to be a mapped erosion area at the southeast driveway property boundary, would this be regulated in any way?  We will utilize existing acces, widened to 20'
4) We will use the existing access and will provide a gated community. Applicant seeks access related comments from City as it relates to emergency service or other requirements.
5) The site is contained within an existing wall, which extends around the Missionary Sisters of Sacred Heart. We plan to keep the wall, with the exception of an opening access to utilities and access. 
6) Attached is a preliminary utility plan.  Applicant is seeking comments.
7) What if any frontage improvements would be required? 
8) The existing home will be demolished, any issues related to demolishing the existing home?
9) Attached is the 6 lot site plan.  The zoning would allow for 11.5 SF residential units. Comments? 
10) Processing Costs - Fees?
